summary: Object processing is central to visual perception, and its neural substrates inform cognitive and computational models of vision. Electroencephalographic (EEG) research has increasingly adopted multivariate pattern analysis (MVPA) to decode distributed neural representations, moving beyond average signal changes and predefined electrodes. title: Stage-Specific Patterns of Imaging and Non-Motor Biomarkers in Spinocerebellar Ataxia Type 3.
summary: Advancements in disease-modifying therapies for spinocerebellar ataxia Type 3 (SCA3) underscore the need for robust biomarkers to monitor disease progression and evaluate treatment efficacy. Although motor phenotypes have been well characterized, less is known about non-motor and imaging-based features across different disease stages. This study aimed to characterize stage-specific patterns of non-motor and imaging biomarkers in SCA3. This cross-observational study included 229 patients with SCA3 and 104 age- and sex-matched healthy controls from the Organization for Southeast China for cerebellar ataxia research. Non-motor symptoms were assessed using a battery of neuropsychological tests.

summary: Organophosphate (OP) poisoning typically manifests in three phases: the acute cholinergic crisis, the intermediate syndrome, and OP-induced delayed neuropathy (OPIDN). Delayed central nervous system sequelae with predominant cerebellar dysfunction are exceptionally rare and poorly characterized. title: Predictive analysis in acute ischemic stroke imaging.
summary: Acute ischemic stroke is a medical emergency that requires rapid diagnosis and treatment to minimize brain damage and improve patient outcomes. Various imaging modalities, such as computed tomography, magnetic resonance imaging, and angiography, play a crucial role in the diagnosis, assessment, and prediction of outcomes in acute ischemic stroke patients. title: Brain-computer interfaces and neuroprostheses for severe speech impairment in amyotrophic lateral sclerosis.
summary: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a relentlessly progressive neurodegenerative disorder that frequently culminates in severe dysarthria and anarthria, profoundly isolating patients and diminishing their quality of life. Traditional speech therapy and conventional augmentative and alternative communication devices rely on residual motor control and become ineffective in late-stage ALS. In response, brain-computer interfaces and speech neuroprostheses have emerged as transformative solutions. However, its tendency to show good sensitivity but limited specificity, particularly in the presence of metastasis, abscess, and other intracranial mimics, is already recognised. title: MRI-Guided Assessment of Rapid Locoregional Progression of Merkel Cell Carcinoma of the Thigh Following Wide Local Excision: A Case Report.
summary: Merkel cell carcinoma (MCC) is a rare and highly aggressive neuroendocrine skin cancer with a marked predilection for elderly and immunosuppressed patients. title: Choroid plexus remodeling associated with inflammatory CSF exposure in preterm acquired hydrocephalus.

summary: Moderate-to-late preterm (MLPT) infants (32-36+6 weeks of gestation) account for approximately 84% of preterm births. title: Right inferior frontal contributions to visual spatial suppression and visuomotor performance.
summary: Elite racket sports demand visuomotor responses at the millisecond level, requiring rapid prioritization of task-relevant information while suppressing competing or redundant signals. title: Terahertz liquid networks: a mesoscopic passive architecture for circumventing physical deadlocks in brain-computer interfaces.
summary: Brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) for major neurological disorders face physical and physiological limitations. title: Factors associated with drug-resistant epilepsy in children with epilepsy: a retrospective cohort study.
summary: Drug‑resistant epilepsy (DRE) remains a major clinical challenge in children. Understanding clinical factors associated with drug resistance is important for guiding management. title: Understanding MEG Source Profiles in Tuberous Sclerosis.

title: An EEG-based framework for Alzheimer's disease diagnosis via single-channel multi-entropy fusion and ensemble learning.

summary: Determine the clinical and imaging correlates and outcomes of lateralized rhythmic delta activity (LRDA). title: Imaging of Neurodegenerative Disorders of the Spinal Cord.
summary: This article aims to provide a comprehensive review of imaging features of non-compressive spinal cord degeneration. summary: This article outlines the evolving role of MRI in traumatic spinal cord injury (SCI) across acute to chronic stages. title: Imaging of Degenerative Cervical and Thoracic Myelopathy.
summary: In this article, we focus on imaging of degenerative cervical myelopathy, the most common form of spinal cord dysfunction in adults arising from its progressive compression by age-related degenerative changes in the spine. title: Genomic structural equation modeling of impulsivity and risk-taking traits reveals three latent factors associated with brain structure and development.

summary: Impulsivity is a multifaceted transdiagnostic trait that emerges in childhood.
